clue.text: Spanish wine? It's not true — at first really casual on detail

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
something not true is a lie

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of really

explanation.surface: A wine buff wonders whether a Spanish wine is genuine, then admits being rather offhand about the details.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Spanish wine?' look like a query; it is just the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cavalier means showing an offhand lack of proper concern, here about the finer points.

clue.text: Addition showing program finish time

parts.note: an app is a computer program
the finish is the end
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A late extra item tacked onto a programme's closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something attached or added on to a larger thing.

clue.text: An offer ultimately unnacceptable: stand fast

parts.note: an becomes the single letter a, the indefinite article
a bid is an offer, as at auction

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of unnacceptable, misspelt in the source

explanation.surface: Faced with an unacceptable offer, the advice is to hold firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide can mean to remain or continue steadfastly in one place or position.

clue.text: Hard to understand strange recitation, Oscar's put off

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet; put off means it is removed

explanation.surface: A baffling recitation at which an actor called Oscar is put off his stride.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from recitation and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate is so complicated or detailed that it is difficult to follow.

clue.text: Colourful display with many different groups involved

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the arc of colours in the sky after rain
second meaning: used of something inclusive of many groups

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the adjective use, as in a rainbow coalition or rainbow nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectral colours, and by extension an alliance or nation embracing many diverse groups.

clue.text: Attractive domestic gets new start

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: homely means domestic, of the home

explanation.surface: A house servant gets a fresh start and becomes rather good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the first; the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old-fashioned word for pleasing in appearance, good-looking.

clue.text: Client having engaged with you initially, needing extra work

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: first letters of Client, having, engaged, with, you

explanation.surface: A client who has hired you up front turns out to be demanding extra effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is witty: chewy food needs extra work from the jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy food takes a lot of chewing, so it needs extra effort from the teeth.

clue.text: Genial, say, with drink, leading to a histrionic show

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: mellow means genial, good-humoured
a dram is a small drink, usually of whisky

explanation.surface: A genial character has a drink and ends up making an overwrought scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational play with exaggerated characters and emotions, a theatrical piece.

clue.text: One unsuccessful in polo series

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of polo and the start of series

explanation.surface: The team that finishes bottom in a series of polo matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is a person who fails to win, someone who is defeated.

clue.text: Introduction of flowers in tulip arrangement gives boost

indicators.note: in places the flower's letter inside the rearranged tulip
an arrangement of letters is a reordering of them, like arranging flowers
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of flowers

explanation.surface: Adding some flowers to a tulip display really lifts the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' reads as flower arranging; it signals the letters of tulip are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a raising of spirits or levels, a lift or improvement.

clue.text: Dreamer, I distribute cards first

parts.note: to deal is to hand out cards
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A card player who fancies themselves insists on dealing first.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty principles, often unrealistically, so is seen as a visionary.

clue.text: New deal, buy inn in a certain way

indicators.note: new indicates the letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh arrangement to purchase a pub is presented as a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Undeniably means in a way that cannot be disputed, certainly.

clue.text: Old craft departs before night

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
Noah's Ark is the old vessel of the Bible

explanation.surface: An ancient boat sets sail before nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark as a noun means the time of no daylight, nightfall.

clue.text: Leading couples in large dinner dance seen as affected

parts.note: the leading couple of letters in large
the leading couple of letters in dinner
the leading couple of letters in dance

explanation.surface: The top pairs at a grand dinner dance look rather pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading couples' sounds like dancing partners; it asks for the first two letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes pretentious, snobbish manners or speech, an affected style.

clue.text: Popular English worker admitting stage is awkward

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A well-liked English labourer confesses to finding the stage clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, so clumsy.

clue.text: Draw back — front's come off weapon in preparatory event

indicators.note: drawing back means taking the word in the opposite direction
the opening letter has fallen away from the word

parts.note: a lance is a knight's weapon

explanation.surface: A knight pulls back as the tip of his lance breaks off before the main contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ritual dance performed before battle to prepare the warriors.

clue.text: Buoyant, go again at exam, assuming legal right

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the second piece is taken inside

parts.note: to resit is to sit an exam again
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A student cheerfully retakes an exam, claiming it is their legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means able to recover quickly, cheerful and springing back like something that floats.

clue.text: Fickle person, one acting badly in church north of Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of puts the first piece above the next
in places the performer within the church

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
Leon is a city in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A poor actor is found in a church north of a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes colour to match its surroundings, so figuratively someone who changes views readily.

clue.text: American hero, Paul, extremely neat, respectful

parts.note: Paul Revere made the famous midnight ride of 1775

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of neat

explanation.surface: A tidy portrait of an American hero, viewed with great respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, feeling or expressing veneration.

clue.text: Nowhere further to climb — potter gets to work with energy

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A potter energetically starts work at a bench, having no more ladders to scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a tree is the highest point a climber can reach on it, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Priest exposing counterfeit article

parts.note: a sham is a counterfeit, a fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A churchman is exposed as a fraud over a forged item.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spiritual intermediary in some cultures, a kind of religious functionary.

clue.text: High point from champion bringing in millions

indicators.note: bringing in means taking the second piece inside the first

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a champion

explanation.surface: A champion's career peaks when they start earning millions.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or summit, the highest level of achievement.

clue.text: Lacking experience in class, move slowly

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
a raw recruit is inexperienced

explanation.surface: A green new pupil in the classroom shuffles along at a snail's pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to proceed at a very slow pace, as traffic does.

clue.text: Sponger's ordeal possibly?

parts.note: a loose, freely arranged form of loader could be the word ordeal

explanation.surface: Is living off others an ordeal for the sponger?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: free signals an anagram of loader, which gives ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader takes advantage of others' generosity without giving anything back, a parasite.

clue.text: In favour of including large, old, puzzle

indicators.note: including puts the following pieces inside the first

parts.note: for means in favour of

explanation.surface: A supporter of a large, antique jigsaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle or confound them completely, as a hard question does.

clue.text: A cover, we hear, to be of use

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a veil is a covering for the face, so a cover is a veil

explanation.surface: A face covering, apparently, comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or benefit, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Restless one in Georgia seen with lawyer before fight

indicators.note: before sets the lawyer ahead of the fight

parts.note: GA is the postal code for the US state of Georgia
a DA is a US district attorney
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A restless type in Georgia is spotted with an attorney ahead of a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person who flits from place to place seeking pleasure.

clue.text: Paint European celebrity by lake

parts.note: a name is a famous person, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: A European star paints beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy paint that dries to a hard finish.

clue.text: Rugby team's unexpected result

indicators.note: an unexpected form of a word is a jumbled one

explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the Irish rugby province based in Belfast.

clue.text: Long to include musical instrument on return, becoming irritable

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

indicators.note: on return means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument
